If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.

The website is live: **https://herding-crashes.streamlit.app**

**What I did:**
- **Deploy settings:** repository `avishj19/can-herding-explain-market-crashes`, branch `main`, file `app.py`, Python 3.14 (the same version every test ran on). The build installed the same package versions as your Mac.
- **Tested on the live server:**
  - Start here loads.
  - The Workspace runs the model and draws the charts.
  - Checks shows the same numbers as on your Mac (median +0.009, passes).
  - Typing `NVDA` fetched live prices from Yahoo, with the last close on 19 November, so Yahoo isn't blocking the cloud server right now.
- **Fixed one thing the live site showed:** on narrow screens the page menu opened over the content. It now opens only on wide screens.
- **README:** it now links to the live site.
- **Commits:** both are named "website demo" and pushed. Streamlit redeploys automatically whenever `main` changes, so future pushes update the site by themselves.

**Things to know:**
- **Waking up:** on the free plan, the site goes to sleep after a few days with no visitors. The first visit after that shows a "wake up" button and takes about a minute. Open it shortly before demo day or your TA's review.
- **Changes to the site:** you can manage it (reboot, logs, settings) at share.streamlit.io under your apps. Code changes just need a push to GitHub.
- **Left for the course:** the video demo, due 1 December. It's at most 5 minutes in your own voice, linked from the README and the website. The README already has a "Video demo: coming" spot for the link.

content.text:
The light/dark switch is live on https://herding-crashes.streamlit.app. I clicked it on the live site and it switched from light to dark.

**How it works for a visitor:**
- **First visit:** the site matches their device. Your Mac is in light mode, so it opened light.
- **The button sits at the top right**, next to Share. In dark mode it reads "☀ Light mode"; in light mode it reads "☾ Dark mode". So it always says what you'll get, not just an icon you have to guess.
- **One click switches everything:** the page, the tables, the controls and every chart (white plot area with dark lines in light mode). The choice is remembered on every page and on return visits.
- **Colors keep their meaning in both modes:** blue fundamentalists, orange chartists, pink herding, green/red gains and losses. In light mode they're slightly darker shades so they stay readable on white.
- **One trade-off:** switching reloads the page, so the Workspace run log starts over. The button's tooltip says so. Streamlit only applies a color set when a page loads, so a full repaint without reloading isn't possible.

**For beginners:**
- **Under every Workspace chart:** one plain sentence saying what it shows and what to look for. For example, under Tail: "the further a line stays up, the more often big moves happen".

content.text:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder or a message from the system confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited, new, failed or never-started call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit unless a call failed or never finished. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

export const meta = {
  name: 'web-app-bug-hunt',
  description: 'Find every bug in the herding web app, fix backend then pages, then break-and-fix until nothing breaks',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Find', detail: '3 read-only finders: backend, Workspace page, other pages + theme' },
    { title: 'Fix backend', detail: 'one agent: herding/, scripts/, tests/ - and move page math into herding/explore.py' },
    { title: 'Fix web', detail: 'one agent: web/ and app.py, calling the backend functions' },
    { title: 'Break', detail: 'adversarial breaker, then a fixer, up to 2 rounds' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'full suite + stress test' },
  ],
}

const CONTEXT = `
Project: a CMU student project, Python, folder is the current working directory. Read CLAUDE.md first (it lists where everything lives).
The web app: app.py (Streamlit 1.67 navigation) + web/ (page_guide, page_story, page_explore = "Workspace", page_compare, page_checks, page_findings, common.py).
All science lives in herding/ (model.py, stats.py, market_data.py, explore.py, kirman.py, ...). herding/explore.py is "the science behind the web app";
tests in tests/test_explore.py. Saved model results: web/numbers.json made by scripts/web_numbers.py. Stress test: scripts/analysis/web_stress_test.py.
web/common.py: per-visitor light/dark palettes via module __getattr__ (c.REAL, c.MIX ...), mode() from st.context.theme / ?mode= / session; a JS button in st.html.
Rules for every agent:
- Never start a server on port 8501 (one is already running). To exercise pages use streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest:
  at = AppTest.from_file("app.py", default_timeout=600); at.run(); at.switch_page("web/page_explore.py").run(); then at.button / at.slider(key=...) / at.radio(key=...) / at.toggle / at.text_input / at.session_state / at.exception / at.dataframe / at.markdown.
  Widget keys in the Workspace: preset, in_a1, in_a2, in_v1, in_days, in_seed, ticker_box, view, frame, t_big, t_dd, t_log, t_earlier, group.
- Do not hit the network in tests: live Yahoo functions take a download= parameter for fakes; for app-level checks you may monkeypatch herding.explore._yahoo / _yahoo_intraday.
- Do not commit, push, or change git state. Do not edit journal/ or docs/papers/.
- Quick test command: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -m "not slow"  (full: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q, about 4 minutes).
`

const BUGS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    bugs: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string', description: 'short unique id, e.g. WS-3' },
      area: { type: 'string', enum: ['backend', 'web'] },
      file: { type: 'string' },
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['crash', 'wrong-number', 'misleading', 'ux', 'duplication', 'minor'] },
      title: { type: 'string' },
      repro: { type: 'string', description: 'exact steps or code that shows it' },
      expected: { type: 'string' },
      actual: { type: 'string' },
      proposed_fix: { type: 'string' },
    }, required: ['id', 'area', 'file', 'severity', 'title', 'repro', 'expected', 'actual', 'proposed_fix'] } },
    checked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'what you exercised and found working' },
  },
  required: ['bugs', 'checked'],
}

const FIXED = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    fixed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, what_changed: { type: 'string' }, test: { type: 'string', description: 'test name that fails before and passes after, or why none' },
    }, required: ['id', 'what_changed', 'test'] } },
    not_fixed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, reason: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'reason'] } },
    files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    quick_suite: { type: 'string', description: 'last line of python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -m "not slow"' },
  },
  required: ['fixed', 'not_fixed', 'files_changed', 'quick_suite'],
}

const FINDERS = [
  { key: 'backend', prompt: `You are a bug FINDER (read-only: do not edit any project file; scratch scripts go in scratch/). Area: the backend.
1. Attack every function in herding/explore.py with edge cases and independent recomputation (empty, length-1, NaN/inf, constant series, negative/zero prices, unsorted or duplicate dates, time-zoned indexes, tiny and huge values, boundary lengths like 499/500/1000/1001, bool passed as int, wrong types). Compare numbers to an independent calculation (scipy, plain loops). Check scripts/web_numbers.py and web/numbers.json agree with fresh model runs for a few seeds, and with figures/RESULTS.md.
2. "Backend is the base": read every file in web/ and app.py and list EVERY calculation done in the page code instead of by a herding/ function - e.g. z-scores / standardizing, drawdown series, range slicing (YTD, 1Y, 5Y, 20Y, intraday fallback), daily-change percent, the dial chart's median/quartiles, mix summaries, closest mix, big-day filtering by range, histogram zero handling, runaway text, the Checks page's percentiles. Report each as a bug with severity "duplication", area "backend", and a proposed function name and signature for herding/explore.py.` },
  { key: 'workspace', prompt: `You are a bug FINDER (read-only: do not edit any project file; scratch scripts go in scratch/). Area: the Workspace page web/page_explore.py.
Drive it headless with AppTest and try EVERY combination: each view (Price, Tail, Histogram, Bursts, Memory) x each range (1D, 7D, YTD, 1Y, 5Y, 20Y, All) x the switches (t_big, t_dd, t_log, t_earlier); every saved market in each group (Stocks, Index funds, Commodities) - especially commodities and the Dow (35k days); every preset then Run model; slider corners (a1 0 and 2, a2 0 and 1, v1 0.5 and 5, every Days option, seed 0 and 10000); several runs in a row and the earlier-runs overlay; the ticker box with good, bad, empty, lower-case, too-short-history and network-failure tickers (monkeypatch herding.explore._yahoo and _yahoo_intraday to fakes, including time-zoned intraday bars and an empty frame); the Live prices switch with Yahoo failing. Look for exceptions, wrong or inconsistent numbers between the stats row / table / charts / sidebar, misleading text, and anything confusing for a beginner.` },
  { key: 'pages', prompt: `You are a bug FINDER (read-only: do not edit any project file; scratch scripts go in scratch/). Area: every page except the Workspace, plus web/common.py and app.py.
Drive pages headless with AppTest (Start here, Story, Compare, Checks, Findings) in BOTH modes: force light/dark by setting at.query_params["mode"] = "light" / "dark" before run, and check the figures' colors come from the right palette (e.g. plot_bgcolor, line colors in the plotly_chart protos or by building the figures directly). Check every number a page prints against a fresh backend calculation (herding/explore.py, web/numbers.json) and against figures/RESULTS.md / docs/KEY_POINTS.md. Check widgets: Compare's pills (none selected, one) and multiselect (empty, 6 markets); Checks' Kirman slider at every value (does the pass rule hold? is the text right at the herding threshold?); Findings' every section and that every image file exists. Check web/common.py: mode() fallback order, module __getattr__ for unknown names and for MIX, the JS button script (read it for bugs: selectors, reload loop, localStorage keys, MutationObserver cost), CSS selectors, thin() on short and tz-aware inputs, tail_axes ranges vs data, dial_chart when the sweep has NaN tails. Also run scripts/analysis/web_stress_test.py --offline and report any failure.` },
]

phase('Find')
const found = await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>
  agent(CONTEXT + '\n' + f.prompt + '\nReport real, reproducible problems only; for each give an exact repro. Also list what you checked that worked.',
    { label: `find:${f.key}`, phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS })))
const allBugs = found.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
log(`Finders reported ${allBugs.length} issues (${allBugs.filter(b => b.area === 'backend').length} backend, ${allBugs.filter(b => b.area === 'web').length} web)`)

const FIX_RULES = `
For EVERY bug: reproduce it first; write a test that fails before your fix and passes after (tests/test_explore.py for herding/explore.py; for page behaviour put AppTest-based tests in tests/test_web_pages.py, marked @pytest.mark.slow if they take more than a few seconds). Prove numbers right against an independent calculation, not against the code itself. Never delete or weaken an existing test to make it pass. If a "bug" is not real, put it in not_fixed with the reason. Keep the existing style: plain-language docstrings, comments that say why. Run the quick suite at the end and report its last line.`

phase('Fix backend')
const backendBugs = allBugs.filter(b => b.area === 'backend')
const backendFix = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the BACKEND FIXER. You may edit herding/, scripts/, tests/ (and web/numbers.json only by rerunning scripts/web_numbers.py). Do NOT edit web/ or app.py - a second agent will switch the pages over after you.
Bugs and duplications to handle (JSON):
${JSON.stringify(backendBugs, null, 1)}
For each "duplication" item: add a well-named, documented, tested function to herding/explore.py that does that calculation (so the backend becomes the base of every number the site shows). List the new functions and exactly which page lines they replace in your what_changed text, so the web fixer can call them.` + FIX_RULES,
  { label: 'fix:backend', phase: 'Fix backend', schema: FIXED })

phase('Fix web')
const webBugs = allBugs.filter(b => b.area === 'web')
const webFix = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the WEB FIXER. You may edit web/, app.py and tests/test_web_pages.py (create it if needed). Do not edit herding/ (if a backend function is missing, report it in not_fixed).
1. The backend fixer added functions to herding/explore.py to replace calculations done in the pages. Their report (JSON):
${JSON.stringify(backendFix, null, 1)}

const backendBugs = allBugs.filter(b => b.area === 'backend')
const backendFix = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the BACKEND FIXER. You may edit herding/, scripts/, tests/ (and web/numbers.json only by rerunning scripts/web_numbers.py). Do NOT edit web/ or app.py - a second agent will switch the pages over after you.
Bugs and duplications to handle (JSON):
${JSON.stringify(backendBugs, null, 1)}
For each "duplication" item: add a well-named, documented, tested function to herding/explore.py that does that calculation (so the backend becomes the base of every number the site shows). List the new functions and exactly which page lines they replace in your what_changed text, so the web fixer can call them.` + FIX_RULES,
  { label: 'fix:backend', phase: 'Fix backend', schema: FIXED })

phase('Fix web')
const webBugs = allBugs.filter(b => b.area === 'web')
const webFix = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the WEB FIXER. You may edit web/, app.py and tests/test_web_pages.py (create it if needed). Do not edit herding/ (if a backend function is missing, report it in not_fixed).
1. The backend fixer added functions to herding/explore.py to replace calculations done in the pages. Their report (JSON):
${JSON.stringify(backendFix, null, 1)}
Switch every page to call those functions, deleting the duplicated page code, and confirm each page still shows the same numbers.
2. Fix these web bugs (JSON):
${JSON.stringify(webBugs, null, 1)}` + FIX_RULES,
  { label: 'fix:web', phase: 'Fix web', schema: FIXED })

phase('Break')
const rounds = []
for (let round = 1; round <= 2; round++) {
  const broke = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the BREAKER, round ${round}. Your only goal is to make the program fail: crash a page, show a wrong or inconsistent number, hang, or mislead a beginner. Read-only: do not edit project files (scratch/ only).
Recent fixes were made in these files: ${JSON.stringify([...(backendFix?.files_changed || []), ...(webFix?.files_changed || []), ...rounds.flatMap(r => r.fix?.files_changed || [])])}. Attack those first, then everything: random sequences of widget changes in AppTest across all pages and both modes (query_params mode), extreme and odd inputs to every herding/explore.py function, the stress test (scripts/analysis/web_stress_test.py --offline), and the full test suite (python3 -m pytest tests/ -q).
Previously fixed issue ids (don't re-report unless they came back): ${JSON.stringify([...(backendFix?.fixed || []), ...(webFix?.fixed || []), ...rounds.flatMap(r => r.fix?.fixed || [])].map(f => f.id))}.
Report only real, reproducible failures with exact repros (area backend or web).`,
    { label: `break:round${round}`, phase: 'Break', schema: BUGS })
  const bugs = broke ? broke.bugs : []
  log(`Breaker round ${round}: ${bugs.length} failures`)
  if (!bugs.length) { rounds.push({ round, bugs, fix: null }); break }
  const fix = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the FIXER for breaker round ${round}. You may edit herding/, web/, app.py, scripts/, tests/ (one agent, so no conflicts). Keep page code thin: calculations belong in herding/explore.py with tests.
Failures to fix (JSON):
${JSON.stringify(bugs, null, 1)}` + FIX_RULES,
    { label: `fix:round${round}`, phase: 'Break', schema: FIXED })
  rounds.push({ round, bugs, fix })
}

phase('Verify')
const verify = await agent(CONTEXT + `
You are the final VERIFIER (read-only except scratch/). Run: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q (full suite, about 4 minutes), python3 scripts/analysis/web_stress_test.py --offline, and an AppTest pass that opens every page in light and dark mode with no exception. Also grep web/ for any remaining calculation that should live in herding/ (z-scores, drawdowns, range slicing, medians/percentiles of model results).
Return a short plain report: exact pass/fail counts, stress-test result line, any page exception, any remaining duplication with file:line.`,
  { label: 'verify', phase: 'Verify' })

return { found: allBugs, backendFix, webFix, rounds, verify }

    x = np.linspace(-8, 8, 2001)

"""Web app: can herding explain market crashes?

import streamlit as st

from web import common

st.set_page_config(page_title="Herding and market crashes", page_icon="📉", layout="wide",

    st.Page("web/page_findings.py", title="Findings", icon=":material/photo_library:"),
]
# every page's address, so the light/dark button can set the mode for pages not opened yet
common.setup(["/" + pg.url_path for pg in PAGES])

nav = st.navigation(PAGES, position="top")
nav.run()
